extracted.intended_audience: researchers and systematic reviewers studying technology-facilitated sexual violence / image-based sexual abuse in young people (ages 12–29)
extracted.subtask_description: A registered systematic-review protocol that specifies eligibility, search, extraction, risk-of-bias, synthesis and grading procedures for identifying quantitative evidence on risk and protective factors for Image-Based Sexual Abuse (IBSA/IBSV) and Technology-Facilitated Sexual Violence (TFSV) in young people aged 12–29.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2×2 predictor taxonomy (level × temporality, online/offline split)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictors are coded on a 2×2 taxonomy (level × temporality) with an online/offline split inside Contextual-Dynamic — cells I-S, I-D, C-S, C-D-online, C-D-offline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cells defined and exemplified: I-S — stable individual traits and historical experience (demographics, Dark Triad/Tetrad, trait empathy/impulsivity, prior victimization, past exposure to domestic GBV, prior consensual sexting); I-D — individual-dynamic cognitive/attitudinal constructs and current behaviours (ambivalent sexism, rape-myth acceptance, moral disengagement, MGRS, aggrieved entitlement, SDO/RWA, hostile masculinity, substance use, cyberbullying co-occurrence); C-S — contextual-static structural features (country, legal framework, family/school structure, community SES); C-D-online — digital-ecosystem exposures (pornography, social-media use, misogynist content, manosphere/incel engagement, problematic internet use); C-D-offline — peer/family/school dynamics (peer norms, parental mediation, concurrent domestic-GBV exposure, school climate, prevention programmes). The taxonomy supports cross-cell co-measurement and mediation/moderation analyses (e.g., [C-D-online → I-D → TFSV/IBSA]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Population eligibility (age)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included studies must report mean age ≤29 or have a ≤29 subgroup reported. The search/population block is anchored to this age band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome scope — TFSV/IBSA subtypes included
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome restricted to sexual-domain technology-facilitated harms (Image-Based Sexual Abuse/Violence and related TFSV types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated eligible outcomes: NCII (non-consensual image distribution), sextortion, cyberflashing, deepfake sexual abuse, coercive sexting, online sexual harassment, image-based sexual harassment, cyber dating abuse with sexual content, online sexual coercion. Umbrella-labelled studies are eligible only if they measure a sexual sub-type (otherwise excluded under code E6_no_sexual_outcome).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design and publication type inclusion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only peer‑reviewed quantitative primary studies from 2014–present are eligible; registers and grey literature are consulted for contextual framing only and are not extracted as primary included studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date range eligibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search and inclusion limited to studies published from 2014 to the present (registry date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Include studies published in English or Spanish (EN/ES).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only EN/ES language studies are eligible for extraction and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy framing (Outcome-anchored Boolean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome-anchored Boolean search: (Outcome block) AND (Population block), no exposure restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches focus on combining explicit outcome terms with the target population; exposures/predictors are not restricted in the search string to avoid missing relevant predictors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Databases and grey literature role
rubrics_metrics.description: Databases searched: Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, MEDLINE, Dialnet, SciELO; registers and grey literature consulted for contextual framing only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registers, theses, preprints and institutional reports are used for contextual framing but are not extracted as included quantitative primary studies; primary extraction is limited to peer‑reviewed articles from the listed databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling umbrella-labelled studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Umbrella-labelled studies (e.g., TFGBV, TF-VAW) are eligible only if they include a measured sexual sub-type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a study uses an umbrella label but does not report any measured sexual outcome/sub-type, it is excluded and coded as E6_no_sexual_outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-reviewer screening with audit mitigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Screening and eligibility decisions performed by a single reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigations include a frozen eligibility vocabulary and blinded self-audits: a 50‑decision self-audit at title/abstract stage and a 20‑decision self-audit at full-text stage to monitor/reduce single-reviewer bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction procedure and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Extraction by single reviewer using a pre-specified structured form with two complementary outputs per included study (a narrative fiche and a pipe-safe CSV row).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both extraction outputs are verified verbatim against the source PDF before being locked; this verification step is intended to ensure extraction accuracy despite single-extractor workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-of-bias assessment tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ROBINS-E, RoB 2, ROBINS-I, or MMAT 2018 as appropriate for included study designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk-of-bias assessments will be summarized using robvis figures. Tool selection depends on study design/type (e.g., RoB 2 for randomized trials, ROBINS-E/ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies, MMAT for mixed-methods where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis approach (SWiM narrative and evidence gap map)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative synthesis following SWiM, organized by predictor taxonomy cell × outcome-type × study design, with creation of an evidence gap map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The synthesis will map which predictors are most studied and their direction/magnitude against TFSV/IBSA, highlight under-studied mediation pathways (especially [C-D-online → I-D → TFSV/IBSA]), and present organization that separates outcome types and study designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis inclusion threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-analysis only conducted if ≥3 comparable effect sizes exist for a predictor–outcome pair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparable effect sizes mean sufficiently similar predictor and outcome definitions and compatible effect metrics; otherwise synthesis remains narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE application criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply GRADE per predictor–outcome pair when meta-analysis/threshold criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GRADE assessments are applied to predictor–outcome pairs (i.e., the same threshold that enables meta-analysis or comparable evidence aggregation triggers GRADE evaluation) to rate certainty of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to PRISMA standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic review follows PRISMA 2020 (and references PRISMA‑P 2015 for protocol standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol and reporting structured according to PRISMA guidelines to ensure transparent reporting of systematic review methods and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected review outputs and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected outcomes: (i) cell-by-cell map of predictors studied and their associations; (ii) evidence gap map highlighting under-studied mediation pathways (notably [C-D-online → I-D → TFSV/IBSA]); (iii) terminological-usage analysis (IBSA/IBSV/TFSV/umbrella labels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review does not hypothesize integrated mediation models but documents empirical gaps; documenting terminological heterogeneity is an explicit objective.
